messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Social behaviour and attitudes, Political behaviour and attitudes, Government, political systems and organisations, and Elections in Germany during the 1990s, matching this research need: German public opinion survey data around the 1998 federal election on party identification, vote intention and recall, coalition preferences, political efficacy, economic expectations, values, EU/national identity, issue competence, and demographics.
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: GESIS German Longitudinal Election Study 1998 Bundestag election pre post survey ZA 1998 party identification coalition
GESIS Politbarometer 1998 cumulative election Germany survey dataset
GESIS German election study 1998 pre election post election ZA dataset economic expectations identity
action.query: GESIS German Longitudinal Election Study 1998 Bundestag election pre post survey ZA 1998 party identification coalition

queries: site:doi.org/10.4232/1 "Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior" "1998"
action.query: site:doi.org/10.4232/1 "Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior" "1998"

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior in Reunified Germany 1998 (ZA3066)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.11968","justification":"Excellent match and the highest-priority dataset for this research. This German national election study contains pre-election and post-election surveys conducted in East and West Germany around the September 27, 1998 federal election. It covers party identification, voting intentions, reported voting behavior, coalition preferences, political efficacy, economic evaluations and expectations, attitudes toward democracy, issue competence, political values, party and candidate evaluations, national identity, European integration, and extensive demographic characteristics. Particularly suitable for examining the relationships between political attitudes, party loyalties, economic perceptions, and electoral choices in 1998."},{"title":"Election Study 1998 (Politbarometer) (ZA3160)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.3160","justification":"Excellent match. This dataset combines monthly Politbarometer public opinion surveys conducted throughout 1998, providing repeated cross-sectional observations before and after the federal election. Topics include first- and second-vote intentions, voting certainty, party identification, coalition preferences, satisfaction with democracy, political interest, government performance, perceived party competence on economic and social issues, economic expectations, attitudes toward European integration and the euro, and demographics. Especially valuable for tracking changes in German public opinion during the 1998 election campaign and subsequent government formation."},{"title":"German National Election Study – Post-Election Study 1998 (German CSES Study) (ZA3073)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.11566","justification":"Excellent match for post-election political attitudes and voting behavior. Conducted following the 1998 German federal election as part of the Comparative Study of Electoral Systems framework, this survey includes party identification, evaluations of political parties and candidates, satisfaction with democracy, assessments of Germany's economic situation, political representation, attitudes toward government and parliamentary institutions, electoral behavior, and demographic information. Particularly useful for analyzing how party attachments, economic evaluations, and perceptions of democratic institutions relate to electoral choices and for comparing Germany with other democracies."},{"title":"Politbarometer 1977–2024 (Partial Cumulation) (ZA2391)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA2391?doi=10.4232%2F1.13431","justification":"Strong supplementary dataset for longitudinal analysis. This harmonized collection of German Politbarometer surveys includes observations from 1998 alongside earlier and later survey years. It provides comparable measures of political attitudes, voting intentions, party preferences, evaluations of political actors, and major political issues. Researchers can isolate the 1998 observations and compare them with preceding elections and longer-term changes in public opinion. It is particularly useful for distinguishing election-specific opinion shifts from enduring patterns of party identification and political behavior. The linked landing page identifies the dataset and its documentation."},{"title":"Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior in Reunified Germany 1994 (ZA3065)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.11973","justification":"Highly relevant comparison dataset. This 1994 federal election study belongs to the same research series as the 1998 election study and uses comparable pre-election and post-election survey designs in East and West Germany. It contains measures of voting behavior, party preferences, political attitudes, democratic evaluations, political participation, economic perceptions, and demographic characteristics. Its principal value is enabling comparisons between the 1994 and 1998 elections, including changes in party identification, government evaluations, political efficacy, and electoral support preceding the 1998 change of government."},{"title":"German General Social Survey (ALLBUS/GGSS) – Cumulation 1980–2023 (ZA8837)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.14696","justification":"Strong supplementary source for social and political attitudes in Germany during the 1990s. The cumulative ALLBUS dataset contains observations from the 1998 survey and other 1990s waves. Its political measures include voting intentions, recalled voting behavior, party identification, political interest, satisfaction with democracy, left-right ideological identification, political efficacy, confidence in institutions, and attitudes toward European and German identity. It also includes economic expectations, social values, national pride, and extensive demographic information. Particularly useful for placing election-related attitudes within broader patterns of social change and for examining relationships between political preferences, socioeconomic position, and values."}]}
